newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see rush of FRNs in dollars and sterling.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see rush of FRNs in dollars and sterling.

text.p: The most popular structure to be launched on Thursday were floating-rate notes, with activity seen in dollars, sterling and marks.

Demand for sterling transactions was driven by the higher returns available there. Bankers said sterling Libor has topped seven percent, and with interest rates expected to rise in Britain, investors wanted to lock in an instrument that would pay higher coupons if rates went up.
"People expect rates to go up, therefore Libor to increase, therefore they buy a floater and ride it on the way up," an FRN trader at a U.S. bank said.
Australian St George Bank launched the largest deal, a 250 million stg five-year senior debt issue. Merrill Lynch also tapped the market with a 75 million stg increase of a July 2002 FRN.
"There is a lot of demand for senior sterling FRNs at the moment and both issues have sold well," a banker involved in the deals said.

In dollars, CIBC Wood Gundy issued a $250 million subordinated 15-year FRN with a call and step-up after 10 years. Bankers said the deal was innovative, with most subordinated paper in the dollar sector having a 10-year maturity with calls after five years.
"CIBC was fairly generously priced, which reflects the fact it is the first such deal," an FRN trader said.
"In the senior debt market we are seeing more seven-year deals instead of five-years, and now in the subordinated debt market maturities are extending to 15 instead of 10 years," he said.
"The market is so tight people are going longer and longer to get the same yield."

Bankers said sentiment on the emerging market side had improved after the U.S. Treasury market became more bullish on remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan which reduced concerns about U.S. inflation.
In New York on Wednesday, Escelsa launched its delayed 10-year bond. The $500 million bond issue was well-received, bankers said.
"The Greenspan comments created an issuance window in the Eurobond market for emerging markets," a dealer in London said.
Escelsa, as well as Argentina, decided to delay their new issues last week as emerging market spreads widened sharply on concerns of a currency devaluation in Brazil.
This week, the market had stabilised, bankers said.
"Sentiment has steadied, and we expect quite a few deals next week, before the August summer holiday," a Eurobond specialist said.
In the pipeline are Axa, Cointel and Argentina, he said.
In Europe, the city of Moscow said it planned to launch a $500 million Eurobond in September or October. It would be its second Eurobond transaction this year.
